PullRequest.Title: Toggle Copilot Dashboard Visibility with Clicks
PullRequest.Body: This pull request implements the functionality to toggle the Copilot dashboard visibility by clicking the status icon in the editor window. The changes ensure that a single click shows the dashboard, while a subsequent click hides it.

RegressionFixes.Mechanism: With the show-only command, every mouse click on an already open Copilot status dashboard first disposed it on MOUSE_DOWN and then immediately rebuilt it on CLICK. Dashboard construction always forced an entitlement refresh that bypassed the fresh-data cache, so attempts to close generated needless DOM/listener/interval churn and a fresh network request.
RegressionFixes.Symptom: Clicking the already-open Copilot status icon caused unnecessary dashboard reconstruction and uncached entitlement network refreshes instead of closing it, adding avoidable network traffic and UI/CPU churn.
RegressionFixes.FixedBehavior: The Copilot status entry now uses ToggleTooltipCommand; when the dashboard was pinned at pointer-down, the click only hides/disposes it. This prevents the close interaction from reconstructing the dashboard component tree, re-registering its listeners/interval, and scheduling another uncached entitlement refresh. Reopening still performs the intentional fresh update.
RegressionFixes.Evidence: Base line 385 assigned ShowTooltipCommand. StatusbarEntryItem's existing managed-hover MOUSE_DOWN handler disposes the visible widget before the CLICK handler executes; ShowTooltipCommand then calls hover.show(), whose triggerShowHover creates a new ManagedHoverWidget and invokes the dashboard content factory. ChatStatusBarEntry's factory instantiates ChatStatusDashboard, whose render() always calls chatEntitlementService.update(token). That reaches forceResolveEntitlement(), which calls defaultAccountService.refresh({ refreshEntitlements: true }); getEntitlements explicitly bypasses its fresh-data cache for that option and performs the entitlement GET. DefaultAccountProvider uses a 100 ms ThrottledDelayer, so only near-simultaneous calls coalesce; ordinary successive clicks can each schedule a fresh uncached request. The changed ToggleTooltipCommand path captures pinned state before MOUSE_DOWN and, on the closing click, hides/disposes instead of calling show().

Scenarios.Scenario: Signed-in user clicks the Copilot status-bar icon to open, close, and reopen the dashboard with a mouse.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Pointer-down performs one capped hover-stack lookup; mouse-down disposes an existing managed hover; click either stops after disposal when closing or synchronously constructs/layouts the dashboard when opening. The entitlement refresh starts during construction but cached quota content renders immediately, so network completion is off the initial visibility critical path and only updates indicators later.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Force-refresh default-account entitlement data with refreshEntitlements=true, bypassing the fresh entitlement cache and issuing the configured entitlement GET.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One logical forced refresh per dashboard construction; normally one successful entitlement GET, with provider/session retries only on failure. Calls arriving within the 100 ms ThrottledDelayer window are coalesced/serialized; ordinary separate reopen clicks each refresh.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Opening performed the same refresh. A click intended to close also disposed and immediately reconstructed the dashboard under ShowTooltipCommand, causing another forced refresh; the diff removes that close-click refresh.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The request is asynchronous and does not block initial dashboard rendering; it affects later quota indicator freshness and consumes network/service capacity.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read the persisted quick-settings collapsed flag during construction; when a resumed quota badge is first opened, asynchronously clear/persist its state.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One synchronous profile-storage read per construction; at most one deferred state write for the resumed state until it is cleared.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same reads/writes occurred whenever the show-only command constructed the dashboard; closing clicks could unnecessarily trigger them through reconstruction, while the diff avoids that work.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The read is on dashboard construction; the resumed-state write is deferred with a zero-delay timeout and is off the immediate click/render stack.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One status entry and a hover stack capped at MAX_HOVER_NESTING_DEPTH=3. Dashboard DOM/listener work scales with the bounded built-in sections plus the current contributed status-entry collection; each construction handles that collection once.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Hover lookups and DOM disposal/construction are synchronous on the UI thread. Entitlement refreshes are funneled through a shared 100 ms ThrottledDelayer rather than running with unbounded concurrency; separate opens can still produce sequential refreshes.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The dashboard renders from current in-memory quota state, but intentionally calls refreshEntitlements=true on every construction, bypassing the fresh entitlement cache. The diff changes closing from a reconstruction/cache-bypassing refresh to disposal only; reopening retains the prior cold/warm behavior.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: event ordering, hover disposal, capped stack lookup, dashboard construction, cache bypass, and refresh throttling are explicit in the call path and covered by added interaction tests.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact dashboard DOM size, contributed-entry count, and entitlement request latency vary by installation/account, but the before/after elimination of close-click reconstruction and forced refresh is directly traced.
Scenarios.Verdict: No regression. The diff reduces repeated synchronous construction and uncached network work on close clicks; opening/reopening retains existing costs.

Scenarios.Scenario: User toggles the Copilot dashboard with keyboard or touch, including from a passive hover/focus preview.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The activation executes one live sticky-hover lookup (stack capped at three), then either disposes the widget or calls managed-hover show. Passive previews are focused without reconstruction when still live; a subsequent close disposes them. Reopening constructs the dashboard and starts the existing asynchronous entitlement refresh.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Forced entitlement refresh when activation creates a new dashboard widget.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Zero requests when activation merely focuses a live passive preview or closes a pinned dashboard; one logical refresh when activation constructs/reopens it, coalesced within the provider's 100 ms throttling window.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Keyboard/touch show-only activation already constructed and refreshed when no widget existed; the diff adds the ability to dispose on a subsequent activation rather than preserving/showing it.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Off the initial UI visibility critical path; current state is rendered first and the promise updates quota indicators later.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Constant work per activation plus a hover-stack scan capped at three; reopening DOM work scales once with current contributed dashboard entries.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Activation handling is synchronous; async refreshes are shared through the default-account update throttler. Listener ownership uses MutableDisposable and managed-hover disposal, so command updates and widget closure do not accumulate handlers or intervals.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Live widget state avoids reconstruction while focusing a passive preview. Once disposed, reopening intentionally bypasses fresh entitlement cache exactly as before; closing performs no refresh.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the new pointer/tap/keyboard branches, bounded lookup, managed-hover lifecycle, and refresh path are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Touch event synthesis differs by browser, but the relevant tap/click paths and live-state fallback are directly covered. Exact remote latency does not affect the no-regression conclusion.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. Added constant-time event work is negligible and lifecycle-bounded, while close activations eliminate retained UI and avoid reconstruction.

Analysis.Summary: Reviewed all 11 changed files and complete diff pages for the performance focus. Traced mouse, keyboard, touch, passive-preview, hover-stack, dashboard construction/disposal, storage, and forced entitlement-refresh paths. No diff-introduced performance issue was found. Recorded the PR's concrete fix for a shipped repeated-work/network regression introduced by e1d07bbeafbe2c795db2b954a4fc4e0d79b88a74.
